function_analysis: Unchanged: (F1) reduce turbulent skin friction (needs effective slip of order one viscous length, ~5 um at 8 m/s); (F2) keep the hull free of biofilm and hard fouling for years without biocides; (F3) survive abrasion, impact, hydrostatic load and UV for several years; (F4) be installable and repairable on ~1e4 m2. Note on evaluation: the steady sublayer Couette model maps a slip length b to a wall-shear reduction b/(H+b); with H = 5 viscous lengths this overstates the turbulent effect about threefold. The linearised turbulent result (DR ~ 2 Delta U+/U_b+) is reproduced by the same Couette model if the gap is H+ = U_b+/2 ~ 18 viscous lengths (~88 um at 8 m/s); the new wall-shear candidate below uses this calibrated gap so that its simulated number is an honest turbulent estimate.
mechanism_classes_considered: other: actively strained soft skin at cm scale (extrapolation of the dolphin elite)
other: polymer drag reduction (Toms effect) from wall-released mucus-like polymer
trapped_gas_or_liquid: closed-cell lubricant grooves refilled by a mm-scale bladder (combination)
graded_stiffness: compliant walls (rejected: small, unreliable turbulent benefit)
analogues_considered: Humpback and grey whale skin: large-scale skin sloughing, and barnacles that are shed with the skin
Fish mucus (e.g. barracuda, Pacific bonito) with drag-reducing high-molecular glycoproteins
Aircraft pneumatic de-icing boots: cm-scale inflatable tubes that crack off ice by strain
Insect tracheal bladders and peristaltic pumping (bladder-driven refill)

candidates.title: Whale-skin cm-bladder panels that peel off juvenile barnacles
candidates.summary: The dolphin skin scaled up tenfold: a 2 mm thick, abrasion-tolerant fouling-release silicone (E ~ 1.5 MPa) spans 20 mm wide pressure-compensated bladders, like the pneumatic de-icing boots of aircraft. A 6 kPa pulse gives the same 15 % edge strain as the mm version (strain depends only on p a^2/(E t^2)), but the thicker skin survives fenders and cleaning, and the cm-scale bulge (about 2 mm) bends the skin under the rigid base plates of juvenile barnacles, producing interfacial shear of order 50-80 kPa, comparable to their critical removal stress on silicone.

back_of_envelope.quantity: skin edge strain and interfacial shear under a rigid barnacle base; friction benefit vs the same static coating after a season of fouling
back_of_envelope.formula: eps_edge = p a^2 (1-nu^2)/(2 E t^2) = 6e3*(0.02)^2*0.76/(2*1.5e6*(2e-3)^2) = 0.152; D = E t^3/(12(1-nu^2)) = 1.32 N m; w_max = p a^4/(384 D) = 6e3*1.6e-7/(384*1.32) = 1.9 mm; shear-lag interfacial stress under a rigid base ~ G eps = 0.5e6*0.15 = 75 kPa vs 20-100 kPa critical removal stress of juvenile barnacles on PDMS; slime plus light calcareous fouling costs ~15-25 % friction (Schultz 2007), so keeping it off saves ~15 %

candidates.main_risk: Adult barnacles and tubeworms that settle during long idle periods without pulsing cement too strongly to be peeled, and a pressure-compensated bladder system over the whole hull is expensive and a leak point.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest known: aircraft pneumatic de-icing boots and static silicone fouling-release coatings; lab studies of dynamic surface deformation at mm scale. New: sizing the bladder so that the skin can be 2 mm thick (hull-durable) while the strain stays above the biofilm threshold, and using the cm bulge to load barnacle base plates in peel, which strain-only microscale approaches cannot do.
candidates.inspiration_source: Whale epidermis sloughing that sheds attached barnacles and cyamids with the skin
candidates.physical_mechanism: A soft thick plate strip clamped at the bladder walls bends under a uniform pulse pressure; the curvature gives edge strain above the biofilm detachment strain and, under a rigid barnacle base, an interfacial shear/peel stress of order G*eps that exceeds the removal stress of young barnacles on silicone. Steady 1D model: clamped-clamped strip deflection w(x) from the known moment distribution; metrics peak strain 16 t w_max/a^2 and w_max.

parameters.name: skin_thickness
parameters.justification: Thick enough to survive fenders and soft cleaning for years.

parameters.name: skin_youngs_modulus
parameters.justification: Filled fouling-release silicone; higher modulus raises interfacial shear under barnacles.

parameters.name: bladder_width
parameters.justification: Larger than barnacle base diameters (5-10 mm) so a whole base sits on the bending zone; a/t = 10.

parameters.name: pulse_pressure
parameters.justification: Above ambient (pressure compensated); gives 15 % edge strain for a/t = 10 and E = 1.5 MPa.

parameters.name: barnacle_removal_stress
parameters.justification: Reported critical removal stress of juvenile barnacles on PDMS fouling-release coatings is ~0.02-0.1 MPa.

candidates.title: Mucus-gland polymer release rows: Toms-effect drag reduction from wall pores
candidates.summary: Rows of 10 um pores every ~10 m along the hull release a concentrated, non-toxic, drag-reducing polymer solution (high-molecular PEO or a fish-mucus-like glycoprotein) into the viscous sublayer, like the mucus glands of fast fish. Near-wall polymer concentrations of a few wppm damp the near-wall vortices (Toms effect) and shift the log law upward by several wall units; the effect decays downstream by diffusion, so injection is repeated.

back_of_envelope.quantity: hull-averaged skin-friction reduction with injection rows every 10 m, and the polymer consumption
back_of_envelope.formula: flat-plate polymer-injection data show 60-80 % DR near the slot decaying to ~20 % after ~10 m; hull average ~20 %; equivalent log-law shift Delta U+ = U_b+ (1/sqrt(0.8) - 1) = 36.5*0.118 = 4.3 -> effective slip b = 4.3*4.8 um = 21 um in a calibrated Couette gap H+ = U_b+/2 (88 um): b/(H+b) = 0.19; consumption: 4000 wppm at Q/(nu*span) ~ 10 -> 4e-5 kg/(s m) per row, 60 m girth, 20 rows -> ~0.05 kg/s ~ 4 t/day

candidates.main_risk: Polymer consumption of order tonnes per day for a large ship costs more than the fuel it saves and discharges large amounts of polymer into the sea; the concept also does nothing against fouling.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest known: polymer injection trials for ships and submarines (1960s-2000s) and fish-mucus drag studies. Hardly new; the only adaptation is micro-pore release into the sublayer from glands distributed in the coating instead of discrete slots, which improves near-wall retention somewhat but does not change the consumption economics.
candidates.inspiration_source: Mucus glands of fast fish (e.g. barracuda, bonito) that release drag-reducing high-molecular glycoproteins
candidates.physical_mechanism: Stretched long-chain polymers in the buffer layer damp streamwise vortices and shift the mean velocity profile upward by Delta U+ (maximum-drag-reduction asymptote not reached). In the steady model this log-law shift is represented as an effective Navier slip length b = Delta U+ * nu/u_tau in a viscous-sublayer Couette flow whose gap is calibrated to H+ = U_b+/2, so that b/(H+b) reproduces the linearised turbulent drag reduction 2 Delta U+/U_b+.

parameters.name: log_law_shift
parameters.justification: Hull-averaged log-law shift corresponding to ~20 % DR with repeated injection; local values near the slot reach 10-15.

parameters.name: viscous_length
parameters.justification: nu/u_tau at 8 m/s on a 200 m hull (u_tau = 0.22 m/s).

parameters.name: calibrated_gap
parameters.justification: H+ = U_b+/2 = 18.3 viscous lengths, which makes the Couette model reproduce the linearised turbulent result.

parameters.name: pore_diameter
parameters.justification: Pores below ~2 viscous lengths release into the sublayer without acting as roughness.

candidates.title: Bladder-refilled closed-cell lubricant skin: pneumatic strokes that shed slime and refill grooves
candidates.summary: Combines the two parents: the closed-cell lubricant grooves (30 um wide, 45 um deep) are moulded into a soft silicone skin (250 um) that spans 2 mm wide lubricant bladders. A pulse of ~3 kPa bulges the skin by ~0.15 mm: the 15 % strain at the ridge crests sheds biofilm, and the bladder stroke pushes lubricant through floor pores into the cells, so every cell is refilled locally from its own mm-scale reservoir instead of a hull-wide distribution network; the grooves between pulses give ~6 % turbulent friction reduction.

back_of_envelope.quantity: stroke volume vs groove inventory, and combined friction benefit vs an untreated hull
back_of_envelope.formula: D = 5e5*(2.5e-4)^3/(12*0.76) = 8.6e-7 N m; w_max = p a^4/(384 D) = 3e3*1.6e-11/(384*8.6e-7) = 0.146 mm; stroke film per area = (8/15) w_max * a/pitch = 0.533*146 um*0.8 = 62 um vs groove inventory 45 um*0.8 = 36 um (one stroke refills all cells); edge strain p a^2 (1-nu^2)/(2 E t^2) = 0.146; friction: ~6 % from closed-cell slip (b+ ~ 1.3) plus avoided slime (~5-10 % averaged over a season) -> ~10 %

candidates.main_risk: Soft silicone ridges and a soft skin under 15 % strain crack at the groove roots or lose their sharp pinning edges, so the lubricant is no longer held and the grooved soft surface fouls and abrades faster than a smooth coating.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest known: lubricant-infused grooves and pneumatic antifouling skins, each on their own. New: the actuation stroke is the refill pump, sized so that one stroke exceeds the groove inventory; this removes the separate feed network of the swordfish parents and keeps the lubricant retained in closed cells, unlike the micro-lid combination whose expelled film was sheared away.
candidates.inspiration_source: Swordfish oil gland (local reservoirs emptied through skin pores) combined with dolphin epidermal sloughing
candidates.physical_mechanism: Clamped soft plate strip over a lubricant bladder deflects under a pulse pressure; the swept volume (integral of w over the bladder width) is pushed through floor pores into the closed-cell grooves on the skin surface, and the curvature strains the surface above the biofilm detachment strain. Between strokes the lubricant-filled closed cells provide Navier slip as in the parent. Steady 1D model: skin deflection w(x) across the bladder; metric: swept lubricant volume per unit area (film thickness) and peak strain.

parameters.name: skin_thickness
parameters.justification: Carries 45 um deep grooves on top and still bends at a few kPa.

parameters.name: bladder_width
parameters.justification: mm-scale reservoirs as in the dolphin parent.

parameters.name: bladder_pitch
parameters.justification: Bladder width plus 0.5 mm support rib.

parameters.name: pulse_pressure
parameters.justification: Pressure-compensated pulse; gives ~15 % strain and a stroke larger than the groove inventory.

parameters.name: groove_inventory_film
parameters.justification: Groove depth 45 um times open fraction 0.8: lubricant volume per unit area to refill.
